findings.title: Migration assumes legacy embed settings always have database rows
findings.body: The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup and, if that is 0, does the same for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Site settings are only persisted when overridden, so a site that never set embed_category (or whose stored value does not exactly match a category name) has no joined row; indexing the empty result raises instead of falling back, aborting the upgrade. The embeddable_hosts lookup below correctly checks cmd_tuples, but these two lookups do not.

findings.title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim, bypassing normalization and using unsafe SQL interpolation
findings.body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values could contain entries such as http://example.com/path (the old SiteSetting check handled those), but this INSERT stores each raw line directly in embeddable_hosts.host, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(referer).host (a bare hostname), so migrated scheme/path entries will never match and previously-allowed sites stop embedding after upgrade. The '#{h}' interpolation also breaks the migration (or injects SQL) if a stored line contains a single quote.

findings.title: Update and destroy return 500 for a missing embeddable host
findings.body: update uses EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host, which immediately calls host.host=; destroy similarly calls host.destroy on the result. A stale or mistyped id (for example a record deleted in another admin tab) yields nil and a NoMethodError/500 instead of a 404 response.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!, and the model has no presence validation. Creating or updating a record without a host (reachable through the new admin API by omitting embeddable_host.host) raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can produce a validation error, turning bad input into a 500. Guard nil and add a presence validation.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration replaces missing records with undefined and discards the ids
findings.body: For *_ids keys the new code maps every id through _lookupSubType and unconditionally assigns the result and deletes the original key. When an id is not present in the side-loaded root collection (or the collection is absent), _lookupSubType returns undefined, so the model property becomes an array containing undefined entries and the original ids are lost. The singular branch only replaces the id when a record was found; the plural branch should likewise preserve ids or omit unresolved entries rather than manufacturing undefined associations (affects embeddable_hosts, colors, and other *_ids payloads).

findings.title: Saved host does not reflect the server-assigned default category
findings.body: When categoryId is null the Rails controller substitutes SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, but the save callback ignores the returned category_id and instead sets category from the stale local categoryId via Discourse.Category.findById(null). The row is then displayed with no category even though the server stored the uncategorized category, and a later edit action dereferences host.category.id (line 26), which can throw for exactly these rows. Use the category_id returned by save (or look the category up from it) before clearing edit mode.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts are allowed, making the per-host category ambiguous
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation on host and the new table has no unique index. An admin (or a double submit) can create two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import can assign imported topics to an arbitrary one of those categories and the result can change as rows are added or removed.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match an incoming referer
findings.body: The format validation on line 2 explicitly permits host values such as example.com:8080 and the before_validation only strips scheme and path, so the port is stored. record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI(host).host, and Ruby's URI#host strips the port, so it compares 'example.com:8080' to 'example.com' and never matches. Such a host validates in the admin UI but can neither embed comments nor determine a category for imported topics; strip the port on save or compare host and port consistently.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators were written to each other's files
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads both files so tests still pass, but the swapped contents are misleading and make it likely a future edit or deletion removes the wrong definitions; move each fabricator into the file named for it.
